open_points.subject: Run spool lifecycle at startup
open_points.text: `store` owns "start-time removal of temporary files and of spools no longer kept"; but `store` "Must not own ... when a run's spool is emptied or released (that is `runs`)".
open_points.question: Which module decides that a specific run spool is "no longer kept" and therefore removable at startup?
options: `runs` decides eligibility and calls a store delete primitive
`store` derives eligibility itself from run/release records and deletes during open
`surface` coordinates and instructs `store` after calling `runs` recovery
open_points.default_guess: `store` derives eligibility from persisted run status/release markers during startup cleanup.

open_points.subject: Pre-send check pipeline for operation sends
open_points.text: `effects` owns "reaching an operation element in the order of A11 rule 1 — pre-send checks..."; `bindings` owns "the stale check before every send"; `service_invoker` owns "the pre-send checks of the instance and the inputs (A09 rule 6)".
open_points.question: Who is the single orchestrator of A09 rule 6 first-failure order and refusal detail across stale-binding, instance/credential, and input-placement checks?
options: `service_invoker` performs all pre-send checks, including stale via callback
Checks are split and `runs` composes outcomes
open_points.default_guess: `effects` orchestrates the ordered checks and delegates subchecks to `bindings`/`service_invoker`.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution writing for operation nodes
open_points.text: `runs` owns "the trace and its order" (A12–A15), while `effects` owns "the in-flight record, the send, the outcome record — approvals ... EffectAttempts and attempt numbers" (A10, A11).
open_points.question: Which module is authoritative for creating operation-node NodeExecution records and enforcing A15 ordering guarantees when operation outcomes are recorded?
options: `effects` writes operation NodeExecutions; `runs` writes function/skip/upstream records
`runs` writes all NodeExecutions; `effects` returns send outcomes only
Both may write NodeExecutions depending on path
open_points.default_guess: `effects` writes operation-node NodeExecutions in its send transaction; `runs` writes non-operation records.

open_points.subject: Execution disclosure class computation (A07 rule 5)
open_points.text: A07 states: "The class of an execution is ... computed from those records, not stored." State 3 assigns masking to `surface` but does not name an owner for this computation.
open_points.question: Which module computes execution class for NodeExecution/TrialExecution when deciding whether to redact `failure_detail` and value payloads for agents?
options: `surface` computes class at response shaping time
`runs`/`functions` compute and expose class in read models
`canonical_values` owns a dedicated execution-class function used by readers
open_points.default_guess: `surface` computes it while serializing responses, using helpers from `canonical_values`.

open_points.subject: State 2 decision A21 security-review gate
open_points.text: A21 requires `design_lint --state 2` to accept "exactly one complete review record", but State 3 module ownership does not assign A21 to any module.
open_points.question: Is A21 implemented by kernel code modules, or is it an external design-time gate with no runtime module owner?
options: External tooling/process only (no kernel module owner)
Owned by `surface` as a startup/runtime gate
Owned by a separate tooling module not listed in State 3
open_points.default_guess: External tooling/process only; no runtime module owner.

open_points.subject: Continuation token refusal responsibility
open_points.text: `surface` owns paging checks (A16), while `store` owns "the one store order of records" and `page_records`; A16 requires refusing "a continuation token that is malformed or names no position of that list."
open_points.question: Who performs the "names no position of that list" check and emits that refusal: `surface` or `store`?
options: `surface` validates both token form and position existence
`store` validates both and returns typed refusal to `surface`
open_points.default_guess: `surface` validates token format, `store` validates position existence against list order.
